tanguar-haor.desc: Tanguar Haor is a protected wetland of international importance, a Ramsar site made up of many beels that merge into one great sheet of water in the monsoon. Swamp trees stand half-submerged, villages sit on raised mounds, and the blue hills of Meghalaya line the horizon. In winter the water retreats and large numbers of migratory ducks arrive. Houseboat trips from Tahirpur used to be the classic way to explore it, but in August 2026 the district administration stopped all houseboats and tourist boats inside the protected boundary until further notice, to protect the wetland.
blocks: How to get there

Bus from Dhaka or Sylhet to Sunamganj town, then by road to Tahirpur. Since 2 August 2026 houseboats and tourist boats may not enter the haor's protected boundary until further notice (Sunamganj district administration).
Good to know

Before planning, check the Sunamganj district administration's latest notice: houseboats and tourist boats inside the protected area are banned until further notice (August 2026). Choose operators with life jackets for everyone, and avoid trips during storm warnings. Carry rubbish back; plastic is a major problem here. Do not swim at night or in deep water.

niladri-lake.desc: Niladri Lake, officially named Shahid Siraj Lake, formed in an abandoned limestone quarry at Tekerghat in Tahirpur. Its water is a vivid blue-green, with small grassy hillocks on its banks and the Meghalaya hills rising just beyond. It is usually visited as part of a Tanguar Haor trip, and sunset here is lovely.
blocks: How to get there
From Tahirpur by boat in the monsoon or by motorbike in the dry season.
Good to know
The lake is deep with steep edges; do not swim without a life jacket. Stay well clear of the border.

pagla-jame-mosque.desc: In the village of Raypur near Pagla bazar, the businessman Yasin Mirza set out to build a mosque like the grand buildings he had admired in Calcutta. Work began in the 1920s and took about ten years, with architects and builders brought from cities across British India. The result is a two-storey, three-domed mosque with a large eidgah in front, standing right on the bank of the Mahasingh river. It is now one of the best-known sights of Sunamganj district and an easy stop on the Sylhet–Sunamganj road.
blocks: How to get there
It is near Pagla bazar on the Sylhet–Sunamganj highway in Shantiganj upazila; any Sunamganj-bound bus or CNG can drop you there, about 30 minutes from Sunamganj town.
Good to know
Dress modestly, and avoid visiting during Friday prayers unless you are joining them.

glance: 295 km to Sunamganj by road, 8–10 hours by bus or car
barikka-tila-jadukata.desc: The Jadukata river emerges from India onto a wide bed of sand and stones in Tahirpur, its water clear and pale blue-green. On its bank rises Barikka Tila, a small hill with grassland, trees and scattered villages. From the top you look down on the river curving out of the hills, with boats loading sand and stone below.
blocks: How to get there
Reach Tahirpur from Sunamganj town, then by motorbike or boat toward Laur/Barikka Tila.
Good to know
Do not cross the border. River currents strengthen after heavy rain in the hills.

lakmachhara.desc: Lakmachhara is a stream near Niladri Lake where water from the Meghalaya hills spreads over a bed of boulders. Visitors sit on the stones in the cool flow and look up at forested hills and cascades on the Indian side. It is far less crowded than the main lake.
blocks: How to get there
A short motorbike ride or walk from Tekerghat/Niladri Lake.
Good to know
Do not cross the border markers. Rocks are slippery, and the stream rises quickly after rain.

shah-abdul-karim-baul.desc: Shah Abdul Karim, born in 1916 in Derai upazila of Sunamganj, became one of the most loved Baul singer-songwriters of Bangladesh, known as 'Baul Samrat'. His songs speak of devotion, social injustice and the life of the haor, and many are standards at gatherings, on radio and in films. Folk festivals in his memory are held in Sunamganj, and his home village of Ujandhol lies on the banks of the Kalni river.

shimul-bagan-tahirpur.desc: Near the Jadukata river, thousands of shimul (red silk-cotton) trees were planted in neat rows on a large plot of land. Around Falgun, in February and March, the trees lose their leaves and burst into crimson blossom, and fallen flowers carpet the ground. It is a short ride from Barikka Tila and a favourite with photographers in spring.
blocks: How to get there
From Tahirpur by motorbike or CNG; often combined with Barikka Tila.
Good to know
Visit in February–early March for flowers; the rest of the year it is just a grove.

glance: Bazars and food hotels in Tahirpur and Sunamganj town
sunamganj-haor-fish.desc: Sunamganj's haors are among the richest freshwater fisheries in Bangladesh. Boats bring in rui, boal, ayre, koi and many small native fish, which are cooked in light curries or fried crisp with turmeric and salt. Eating fish caught the same day, by the haor is one of the pleasures of the trip.

glance: Food hotels in Sunamganj town and Tahirpur bazar
sunamganj-haor-duck.desc: Large flocks of ducks are herded across the haor waters of Sunamganj, feeding on snails and small fish. Their meat is cooked into a dark, spicy curry with plenty of onion, garlic and whole spices, often with rice or chitoi pitha.

glance: Hason Raja Museum in Sunamganj town; folk performances in the region
hason-raja-songs.desc: Hason Raja was a wealthy landowner of Sunamganj who turned from a life of pleasure to mysticism, composing hundreds of songs about the transience of life and longing for the divine. His songs, in simple Sylheti-flavoured Bangla, remain hugely popular in Bangladesh and India. In Sunamganj town, his family home has been turned into a museum with his belongings and manuscripts.

glance: 295 km to Sunamganj by road, 8–10 hours by bus or car
hason-raja-museum-sunamganj.desc: Hason Raja (1854–1922), the zamindar-poet whose mystical songs are still sung across Bangladesh, came from the Tegharia area of Sunamganj. The family homestead by the town is now a small museum showing things that belonged to him, such as clothes, a chair and table, a walking stick, a sword, wooden sandals and handwritten songs. The house you see was built by later generations, since his own mud house is long gone. His grave lies close to the homestead.
blocks: How to get there
In Sunamganj town; a rickshaw or auto from the town centre takes a few minutes to Tegharia.
Good to know
Opening is irregular, so ask locally or phone ahead. Don't confuse it with the Museum of Rajas' in Sylhet city, which is run by another branch of the family.
